title: Training hard but not building muscle? Three common reasons, from the research:
hook: Training hard but not building muscle? Three common reasons, from the research:
caption:
Training hard but not building muscle? Three common reasons, from the research:

Not enough protein. A review of 49 studies found extra protein helped muscle gains up to about 1.6 g per kg of bodyweight a day.

Not eating enough. In a 2022 review, lifters eating too little gained less muscle.

No progression. Doing a little more over time worked in an 8-week study of 43 lifters.

Sources: Morton et al., BJSM 2018. Murphy & Koehler, Scand J Med Sci Sports 2022. Plotkin et al., PeerJ 2022. General information, not medical advice.

title: Stop chasing heavier weights. Start focusing on better repetitions. 💪🔥
hook: Stop chasing heavier weights. Start focusing on better repetitions. 💪🔥
caption:
Stop chasing heavier weights. Start focusing on better repetitions. 💪🔥

One simple tweak that can make a huge difference in your muscle growth is CONTROLLING YOUR REPS.

Your goal shouldn’t be to finish every set as quickly as possible. Focus on:

✅ Lift with control and intention.
✅ Lower the weight slowly.
✅ Maintain proper technique.
✅ Avoid using momentum or swinging.
✅ Work through a full, comfortable range of motion.

Remember, more weight doesn’t always mean more muscle. Quality repetitions, progressive overload, proper nutrition and recovery are what help you build long-term results.

title: High volume vs low volume: which is right for you? 💪
hook: High volume vs low volume: which is right for you? 💪
caption:
High volume vs low volume: which is right for you? 💪

Both work, as long as every set is taken with high intensity (0–2 reps left in the tank).

🔸 High volume: more sets, more muscle growth, but longer sessions and more recovery needed.

🔸 Low volume: fewer sets, quicker sessions and similar strength gains, with less fatigue. Great if you're busy or have a demanding job.

The best plan is the one that fits your life and that you actually enjoy.

A little reminder that the number on the scale doesn’t tell the whole story.

These photos are a few years apart, and while my weight has barely changed, my body composition, strength, and confidence have.

Building muscle takes time. Progress isn’t always linear, and it definitely isn’t always reflected on the scale.

If you’re on your own fitness journey, don’t let a number determine how you feel about your progress. Focus on getting stronger, staying consistent, and celebrating what your body is capable of.
